facts.text: Glencoe began as a 19th‑century rural settlement along Bayou Teche, growing with the river’s role in trade after the 1803 Louisiana Purchase.
Glencoe’s culture reflects the Acadian and Creole heritage that shapes south‑central Louisiana, even though detailed local records are scarce.
Glencoe sits on a low‑lying plain, only about nine feet above sea level, typical of the Atchafalaya Basin’s flat terrain.
Glencoe lies in a parish where 92% of land faces flood hazards, with storm surges reaching nine feet and river flooding common.
In the late 1950s, a state road near Glencoe was straightened to cut railroad crossings, improving safety along the Bayou Cypremort corridor.
The surrounding swamps are 41% forested wetlands with cypress and hardwoods, while 24% are marshes that host alligators and migratory birds.
